## Summary

Refresh the maintained documentation around the verified v0.2.1 release and the accepted rolling workflow.

```diff
- Source-only usage; image publication and anonymous access described as pending
+ Published Linux/amd64 version/digest commands, scan evidence and retained-image retry
- Initial self-release and setup-only Pages status
+ Subsequent exact-tag cycles, observed metadata checks and successful public Pages deployment
- Approval/receipt completion guidance mixed with the active rolling workflow
+ Clear core workflow, recovery/upgrade instructions and separate integration API boundaries
```

Update README, contributing guidance, component/operations pages and site navigation. Preserve historical evidence and distinguish fixture coverage from observed live results.

## Evidence

- **Before:** maintained guides still said no OCI image was published, a real subsequent bumping cycle remained unobserved and Pages deployment was only an intended destination.
  **After:** link the v0.2.0/v0.2.1 proposal/tag runs, [first GHCR publication](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/43929562742/attempts/1), [authorized retained-digest retry](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/43929562742/attempts/2), and [successful Pages build/deployment](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/43929428955).
- `pnpm verify`: passed formatting, type-aware lint, types, all 744 tests and documentation build.
- Normal commit hooks: formatter, full checks (744 tests and docs build), and commit-message validation passed.
- Rendered-site inspection: 24 HTML pages, 1,045 internal links checked, zero missing pages/anchors.
- Inspected tagged snapshots: v0.2.0 uses v0.1.0 and PRs #66/#67/#68/#70/#71; v0.2.1 uses v0.2.0 and PR #72. The v0.1.0 changelog section is preserved byte for byte in both later tags.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: users
summary: Document the published CLI and current release operations.
impact: Readers can use verified digest-pinned installation commands, find recovery guidance and distinguish observed release behavior from remaining validation gaps.
required_action: null
```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Documentation and navigation changes are reversible.

**Blast Radius:** documentation

No CLI, workflow, dependency or settings changes. Package settings could not be independently audited because the available API credential lacks read:packages; anonymous pulls were verified directly. The pull client had empty Docker authentication and no cached release image, but some layers were cached. Controlled conflict/uncertain-write/race exercises and independent consumer adoption remain outstanding.

pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Release proposals now show when inputs were captured, credit captured PR authors, show the recorded capture date beside the version, use fixed section emojis, and link the baseline tag to the captured source SHA. An optional `backfill` command previews enrichment of existing released sections; only `--write` changes `CHANGELOG.md`.

```text
collect / roll → schema-5 capture → deterministic enriched changelog
same evidence on retry          → retain original capture; no PR write
backfill --dry-run              → preview historical enrichment
backfill --write                → replace CHANGELOG.md after edit checks
```

Legacy schema-3/4 snapshots retain their original replay and rendered bytes. Normal refresh preserves released history. Backfill uses current GitHub PR authors and verified local release tags, preserves authored prose and untagged pending blocks, and never invents old capture timestamps. A still-owned release is backfilled only when its local version tag contains the exact committed pending block; conflicting content fails. A fixed spacer separates internal maintenance from the comparison link. Historical dates preserve existing values or recorded capture times, then fall back to the annotated tag date or the tagged commit committer date for lightweight tags. Fallbacks use UTC and an explicit source label.

Closes #75.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: users
summary: Add capture timestamps, contributor credits, section emojis and full comparison links to changelogs, plus an optional command to enrich existing releases with recorded tag-date fallbacks.
impact: Readers can see the captured release context and inspect underlying changes; maintainers can preview historical enrichment before explicitly applying it.
required_action: null
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** Changelogs omitted capture time, author credits, section icons and comparison links. Introducing capture time initially caused an identical rolling retry to refresh its PR (753/754 tests passed).
  **After:** Reconciliation retains the original capture for unchanged evidence; all 44 focused proposal/rolling tests pass, including changed-author refresh coverage.
- The required commit hook ran `pnpm check` with `npm_config_verify_deps_before_run=false`: formatting, type-aware lint, TypeScript, all **758 tests** with coverage, and the documentation build. The environment setting disables automatic dependency reinstallation; all checks run.
- Packaged CLI tests cover offline enriched rendering, backfill preview, explicit writes and repeated output. Tests use temporary Git repositories and mocked HTTP; replay is exercised with network and current-clock access disabled. The actual repository changelog also passed the tagged-Fixes, comparison-spacing and deterministic-date repro with HTTP mocked and no file writes. Live backfill was not performed by this session.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way

Code can be reverted. New schema-5 captures need a compatible pinned tool; legacy captures remain supported. Historical changes require the explicit backfill write command and ordinary diff review.

**Blast Radius:** Changelogs

Presentation and capture evidence change; membership, classification and version decisions remain unchanged. Backfill requires GitHub read access and complete trusted local tags. It preserves untagged pending sections and cannot reconstruct historical capture times. New proposal dates come from captured inputs. Backfilled dates may use labelled immutable tag/commit evidence; the current clock is never used as a historical fallback.

## Summary

Add an opt-in `release-log/ai` library API for bounded text generation through AI SDK Core. It supports explicit OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible connections, including a configured Ollama endpoint. Add local environment examples and ADR 0002 recording the decision. Include a tracked `pnpm notes:preview [version]` development helper that selects an actual changelog section, supports an offline `--dry-run`, and prints a review draft through the configured provider.

```text
explicit configuration + runtime key
  → release-log limits and validation
  → AI SDK direct provider
  → complete, untrusted text + usage
```

Closes #80. This is the provider prerequisite for #76 with a source-checkout development preview. Captured-input release notes, safety-coverage validation, reviewed artifact retention and publication remain separate.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: users
summary: Add optional text generation through explicitly configured AI providers.
impact: Integrations can use vendor APIs or a compatible local model endpoint while ordinary release commands remain independent of AI credentials.
required_action: null
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** no shared generation API or provider integration.
- **After:** real SDK adapters run against synthetic HTTP fixtures for all four provider configurations, including bounds, authentication, cancellation, deadlines and malformed/incomplete output. The packed library also generates through a fixture after an offline production install.

## Verification

- Offline frozen dependency installation succeeded in the isolated worktree.
- After preserving the concurrent main-branch integration, `pnpm verify` passed on the combined branch: formatting, lint, strict types, all 768 tests with coverage, and the docs build. `pnpm notes:preview v0.2.0 --dry-run` selected the expected real changelog section without a provider request.
- Required pre-commit `pnpm check` passed: formatting, type-aware lint, strict TypeScript checks, all 768 tests with coverage reporting, and the documentation build. The commit-message hook also passed. No hooks were bypassed.
- Local live OpenAI verification on 2026-11-16: after the owner linked subscription API credits, one explicit synthetic smoke request succeeded with HTTP 200 and returned `CSV exports now retain the selected rows.` Reported usage: 34 input tokens, 58 output tokens; exactly one API request, with no automatic retries. Two earlier explicit attempts returned HTTP 429 with confirmed `credit_balance_exhausted` / `insufficient_quota`; the diagnostic also confirmed that the request used the key loaded from `.env` without exposing it. This proves one successful OpenAI generation, not live Azure/Anthropic/Ollama behavior or broader model quality. No Docker smoke test was run. Network use also included dependency retrieval, documentation research and GitHub issue/PR operations.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. **Blast Radius:** dependencies and optional generation.

AI SDK 6 is intentionally pinned with a declaration-only `provider-utils` patch to preserve strict TypeScript checks; compiled SDK JavaScript is unchanged. The patch and workspace settings are included in the package for reproducible offline installation. Reassess both on upgrades.

The dependency lock changes the existing snapshot normalizer identity. Prior captures require their original pinned tool; adoption of this revision requires fresh capture/review. No provider/model is enabled by default, retries/fallback and telemetry are disabled, and subscription-backed execution/Gateway routing are deferred.
